title: GPU budget for video ranking
scenario: Size the GPU fleet for the ranking stage of a video recommender, and its cost per 1,000 requests. All values are illustrative assumptions. Use 86,400 seconds per day. Anything within 25% counts.

givens.label: Home-screen loads per viewer per day
Candidates one GPU scores per second

questions.prompt: GPUs needed at peak, with headroom
Ranking cost per 1,000 requests, averaged over a day (fleet sized for peak)

solution:
1. **Peak requests:** 100M × 5 = 500M per day ÷ 86,400 ≈ 5,787 per second on average, × 3 ≈ **17,400 at peak**.
2. **GPUs:** 17,361 × 500 = 8.68M candidates per second ÷ 200,000 ≈ 43.4 GPUs, × 1.5 ≈ **65 GPUs**.
3. **Cost per 1,000 requests:** 65 GPUs × $2 = $130 per hour. On average the fleet serves 5,787 × 3,600 ≈ 20.8M requests per hour, or 20,833 thousand. $130 ÷ 20,833 ≈ **$0.0062 per 1,000 requests**. Because the fleet is sized for peak, autoscaling it down at night is the biggest cost lever.
